note: The English teen edition quotes the ESV (and the WEB for Psalm 68:31) in each chapter's epigraph. That wording cannot be carried into Swahili, so every epigraph was rendered in the Swahili Union Version (SUV) tradition the shipped sw corpus quotes, and the “(ESV)”/“(WEB)” label was dropped. Where a shipped *.sw.json carries the SUV words they were pasted verbatim and the row is `mined` with that file; otherwise the row is `self_rendered` in the SUV register and needs a native check (Proverbs 24:11, Psalm 119:130, Colossians 2:8, Psalm 82:3, Psalm 68:31).

Psalm 68:31 follows the SUV's “Kushi” for Ethiopia. Chapter 12's body echoes the verse as Amanda heard it (“Is not Ethiopia stretching out her hands to God?”), rendered “Je, Kushi haimnyoshei Mungu mikono yake?” and glossed in the same sentence as “Kushi, yaani Ethiopia”.

Chapter 11: the critics' 1 Corinthians 14:34 is self-rendered in the SUV register (“Wanawake wenu wanyamaze katika makanisa”); Amanda's retort “Let your men keep silence in the church” is her own pointed adaptation of the same chapter (cf. 14:28), rendered as the parallel “Wanaume wenu na wanyamaze katika kanisa” and not recorded as a verse.
Chapter 5: the English's bare resolve “I WILL” (after “Pray once more”) needs a verb in Swahili and is rendered “NITAOMBA” (I will pray) — a translator's choice for review.

Clock times are CONVERTED to Swahili reckoning, matching amanda-smith-autobiography-children.sw (one or two in the morning → saa saba au saa nane usiku). Names follow the sw children's edition (Samuel Berry, Bi Celie, Bob → Bob Mdogo); “Mother Jones” is kept in English.
Each chapter's three study questions are translated in the same order; the book's eight Q&A pairs likewise.
